Specification: This specification models a simple multi-car elevator system with a set of people, a set of elevators, and a bounded set of floors. It defines how people choose destinations, call elevators, enter and exit cars, how elevators open and close doors, move, stop, and are dispatched to calls using a simple nearest-eligible-elevator policy rather than a globally optimized scheduling algorithm. The specification includes type and safety invariants, temporal liveness expectations that calls are eventually serviced and waiting people eventually reach their destinations, and fairness assumptions over the main actions; it culminates in a theorem asserting that under Spec, the type, safety, and temporal invariants always hold.
IfThenElse: IF f1 > f2 THEN f1 - f2 ELSE f2 - f1
IF \E e \in Elevator : /\ CanServiceCall[e, call] /\ ElevatorState[e].doorsOpen THEN ActiveElevatorCalls ELSE ActiveElevatorCalls \cup {call}
IF p \in gettingOn THEN [PersonState[p] EXCEPT !.location = e] ELSE PersonState[p]
IF p \in gettingOff THEN [PersonState[p] EXCEPT !.location = eState.floor, !.waiting = FALSE] ELSE PersonState[p]
IF eState.direction = "Up" THEN eState.floor + 1 ELSE eState.floor - 1
IF closest \in stationary THEN [ElevatorState EXCEPT ![closest] = [@ EXCEPT !.floor = c.floor, !.direction = c.direction]] ELSE ElevatorState

[Elevator -> [floor : Floor, direction : ElevatorDirectionState, doorsOpen : BOOLEAN, buttonsPressed : SUBSET Floor]]
[p \in Person |-> IF p \in gettingOn THEN [PersonState[p] EXCEPT !.location = e] ELSE PersonState[p]]
[p \in Person |-> IF p \in gettingOff THEN [PersonState[p] EXCEPT !.location = eState.floor, !.waiting = FALSE] ELSE PersonState[p]]

[floor : Floor, direction : ElevatorDirectionState, doorsOpen : BOOLEAN, buttonsPressed : SUBSET Floor]
ChoiceExpr:
CHOOSE e \in stationary \cup approaching :
            /\ \A e2 \in stationary \cup approaching :
                /\ GetDistance[ElevatorState[e].floor, c.floor] <= GetDistance[ElevatorState[e2].floor, c.floor]
LeadsToOp: c \in ActiveElevatorCalls ~> \E e \in Elevator : CanServiceCall[e, c]

TemporalAssumptions is placed in TemporalProperty because it is a conjunction of WF_/SF_ fairness conditions, which are temporal formulas even though they do not use [], <>, or ~> literally.

FunctionConstructor entry "[floor : Floor, direction : Direction]" is a record constructor syntax that also appears in FunctionConstructor in V2; for the required subdivision it is placed in FunctionConstructor_SetType by elimination as a non-|-> function-like constructor form.

UnchangedExprs contains "UNCHANGED <<PersonState, ActiveElevatorCalls, ElevatorState>>" rather than "UNCHANGED Vars". Although Vars is the tuple variable operator, the file writes the explicit tuple, so it is classified under UnchangedExprs_Explicit.
CloseElevatorDoors and StopElevator contain ENABLED, but they are actions and therefore remain only in ActionDefNames, not in StatePredicate.

TemporalNesting is false. No temporal operator appears explicitly nested inside another temporal operator in the file text; ~> appears in TemporalInvariant, [] appears in Spec and the theorem, and fairness operators appear separately.
